rationale:
Split into four children: three comparator-accepted declarations reused with byte-identical frozen types, and one new pure measure-theory lemma. Depth 4 is below the limit 6.

Why split. The supplied proof has two independent parts.
(A) Steps 1–2 combine the mass triangle inequality M_V(X + cY) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y) with M_V = μ(V) on open V ⊆ U.
(B) Steps 3–6 extend an inequality between measures from open subsets of U to all Borel sets. They use concentration on U, finiteness on compact subsets of U (IMRep facts), outer regularity of finite restrictions, and a compact exhaustion.
The current/IMRep ingredients of (A) and of steps 3–4 already exist as accepted declarations in other branches. This node may use only its children and its depends_on (prerequisites = children + depends_on), so without a split its prover would have to reprove them. The measure theory in (B) is a self-contained statement about abstract measures, reusable wherever an inequality between weights is known on open sets. It is the only new formal work. No existing DAG declaration states it:
- cmc_ml_measure_eq_of_eq_on_open_subsets is an equality version for subsets of O;
- lcmp_measure_le_add_of_open_nhds only treats compact E;
- SimonGMT Chapter01 weaklyRegular_of_closedSetsAreGDelta_of_open_cover needs a global finite open cover and is outside the contract's import closure.

(i) μ(Uᶜ) = 0: Uᶜ ⊆ R_Z.carrierᶜ (carrier_subset), and child 3(d) gives R_Z.measure(R_Z.carrierᶜ) = 0 (step 3).

subproblems.title: Triangle inequality for local mass: M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y) when Z = X + cY on forms supported in G, |c| ≤ 1 (reused accepted lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U, G ⊆ ℝ^P, X, Y, Z ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (contract GeometricCurrentOn U k) and c ∈ ℝ with |c| ≤ 1, and suppose Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G. Then M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y), where M_G is the SimonGMT local mass massOn (supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (X Y Z : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (c : ℝ), |c| ≤ 1 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ⊆ G → Z ω = X ω + c * Y ω) → Z.massOn G ≤ X.massOn G + Y.massOn G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected parent proof ("each admissible ω gives Z(ω) = X(ω) + cY(ω) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y), as ±ω is admissible"; fact (F4) of the grandparent proof), with the identity Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) required only for forms supported in G. This is the comparator-accepted declaration lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.mass_triangle-a1, candidate commit c7dea4b8), reused with its identical frozen type. The proof below is the parent's step 1 written out; it agrees step by step with that node's accepted proof.

Notation. For a k-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm). A form ω is admissible for G if ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (SimonGMT massAdmissibleOn U k G). M_G(T) = T.massOn G = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω admissible for G} ∈ [0, ∞], so ofReal T(ω) ≤ M_G(T) for every admissible ω (SimonGMT le_massOn).

1. Let ω be admissible for G. Then −ω is admissible for G: −ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω ⊆ G, and |(−ω)(x)| = |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, because the Euclidean coefficient norm satisfies |−α| = |α| (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. By step 1 and the definition of M_G as a supremum, ofReal X(ω) ≤ M_G(X), ofReal Y(ω) ≤ M_G(Y) and ofReal Y(−ω) ≤ M_G(Y). Since Y is linear, Y(−ω) = −Y(ω). Now |Y(ω)| is either Y(ω) or −Y(ω) = Y(−ω), so in both cases ofReal |Y(ω)| ≤ M_G(Y).
3. Since |c| ≤ 1, c·Y(ω) ≤ |c·Y(ω)| = |c|·|Y(ω)| ≤ |Y(ω)|. As tsupport ω ⊆ G, the hypothesis gives Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) ≤ X(ω) + |Y(ω)|. The map ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is monotone and satisfies ofReal(p + q) ≤ ofReal p + ofReal q for all real p, q (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le). Hence, by step 2, ofReal Z(ω) ≤ ofReal X(ω) + ofReal |Y(ω)| ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y).
4. M_G(Z) is the supremum of ofReal Z(ω) over all ω admissible for G. By step 3 each of these values is at most M_G(X) + M_G(Y). Hence M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y). ∎
proof_key_steps: For ω admissible for G, −ω is admissible too (same support, |−α| = |α|), so ofReal |Y(ω)| ≤ M_G(Y).
Since |c| ≤ 1, c·Y(ω) ≤ |Y(ω)|. Hence ofReal Z(ω) ≤ ofReal X(ω) + ofReal |Y(ω)| ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y).
Take the supremum over admissible ω.

subproblems.title: Simon 6.3.2(3): on open sets the mass of an integer multiplicity current equals its weight measure (reused accepted dtc_mass_eq_measure)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for every open W ⊆ U, M_W(T) = μ_R(W), where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is Simon's mass 6.2.5 with the Euclidean coefficient norm (the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y) and μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M = R.measure; both sides are taken in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → R.Represents T → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance: comparator-accepted declaration dtc_mass_eq_measure (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.mass_eq_measure-a1, candidate commit bff81d31), reused with its identical frozen type. It is also the selected node's declared, already resolved dependency. In the selected parent it is step 2 ("For open V ⊆ U the sibling mass_eq_measure gives M_V(•) = μ_•(V)"). It is re-listed here so that the four child conclusions alone imply the parent. The numbered proof below is that node's accepted parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim. Its 'Source' line and the phrase 'the parent proof' refer to that node's original parent.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–766, stated there without proof) together with 2.4–2.8 (lines 222–283); this is the identity "M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W" quoted at the start of the parent proof. Notation: for α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector), |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P}; e^I ∈ Λⁿ is the covector e^I(v₁,…,vₙ) = det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; μ := μ_R, so μ(B) = ∫_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for Borel B. By definition M_W(T) = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(y)| ≤ 1 ∀y} ("admissible" forms).
1. Algebraic lemma. Let τ₁,…,τₙ ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal, σ ∈ {1, −1}, and let ζ ∈ Λₙ (MultiVector) satisfy ζ(α) = σ·α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for all α. For increasing I put d_I := det(⟨e_{I(a)}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b} = e^I(τ₁,…,τₙ). (a) Expanding each τ_b in the standard basis and using multilinearity and the alternating property (terms with a repeated basis vector vanish, the others are grouped by their increasing rearrangement with the sign of the sorting permutation) gives α(τ₁,…,τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·d_I for every α. (b) By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I d_I² = det(AᵀA), A the P×n matrix with columns τ_b; AᵀA = I_n by orthonormality, so Σ_I d_I² = 1. (c) Hence, by Cauchy–Schwarz, |ζ(α)| = |Σ_I α(e_I)d_I| ≤ |α| for every α. (d) Put α_ζ := Σ_I ζ(e^I)·e^I (a linear function of ζ). Since e^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing I, J, α_ζ(e_J) = ζ(e^J) = σd_J, hence |α_ζ| = (Σ_J d_J²)^{1/2} = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = Σ_I ζ(e^I)² = Σ_I d_I² = 1.
2. By the field `orients` of R there is an Hⁿ-null set Z ⊆ M such that for every x ∈ M ∖ Z, ξ(x) satisfies the hypothesis of step 1 (τ an orthonormal basis of the approximate tangent space T_xM). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable on M (ξ is, ω is continuous, evaluation is continuous bilinear) and bounded by θ(x)·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}(x) off Z; since tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, ∫_{M∩tsupport ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (field `locallyIntegrable_mult`). So T(ω) is the integral of an integrable function.
3. Upper bound. Let ω be admissible. For x ∈ M ∖ Z, step 1(c) and tsupport ω ⊆ W give θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) ≤ θ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ θ(x)·1_W(x). Integrating, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ(W), so ofReal T(ω) ≤ μ(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. Lower bound on a compact set. Let K ⊆ W be compact and 0 < ε < 1. Fix s > 0 with K₁ := {y : dist(y, K) ≤ s} ⊆ W; K₁ is compact, K₁ ⊆ U, so μ(K₁) < ∞.
 (a) The open sets V_m := {dist(·, K) < 1/m} decrease to K and μ(K₁) < ∞, so for some m with 1/m < s the open set V := V_m satisfies K ⊆ V ⊆ K₁ and μ(V ∖ K) < ε.
 (b) Let α(y) := α_{ξ(y)} (step 1(d)); α is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, so there is a Borel map α̃ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ with α̃ = α μ-a.e. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, μ-null subsets of M are Hⁿ-null; let Z' be a Borel Hⁿ-null set containing Z ∪ ({α̃ ≠ α} ∩ M). For y ∈ M ∖ Z' we have |α̃(y)| = 1 and ξ(y)(α̃(y)) = 1. By Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure μ⌞K₁ on ℝ^P (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; Λⁿ is identified with ℝ^{C(P,n)} through the coefficients α(e_I)) there is a compact F₀ ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ F₀) < ε/2 and α̃|_{F₀} continuous; by inner regularity there is a compact F ⊆ (F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z' (a Borel set, M being Borel) with μ(((F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z') ∖ F) < ε/2. As μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and μ(Z') = 0, μ(K ∖ F) < ε; moreover F ⊆ M ∖ Z', α̃|_F is continuous, and |α̃| = 1, ξ(·)(α̃(·)) = 1 on F.
 (c) By the Tietze extension theorem (coefficientwise) α̃|_F extends to a continuous β₀ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ. Let r(v) := v / max(1, |v|), the continuous radial retraction of (Λⁿ, |·|) onto its closed unit ball, and β := r ∘ β₀. Then β is continuous, |β| ≤ 1, and β = α̃ on F (because |α̃| = 1 there).
 (d) Let φ_δ be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_δ = 1, support in B_δ(0)) and β_δ := β * φ_δ (coefficientwise convolution). Then β_δ is smooth, |β_δ(y)| ≤ ∫|β(y − z)|φ_δ(z) dz ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm, Minkowski's integral inequality), and β_δ → β uniformly on compact sets as δ ↓ 0 (β is uniformly continuous on compact sets). Fix δ with |β_δ − β| ≤ ε on F.
 (e) Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(V) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K (smooth Urysohn lemma), and set ω := χβ_δ. Then ω is smooth with compact tsupport ⊆ V ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and |ω| ≤ 1: ω is admissible.
 (f) Since χ = 1 on F ⊆ K and ω = 0 off V, T(ω) = ∫_{F} θ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ + ∫_{M∩(V∖F)} θ χ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ. For y ∈ F (so y ∈ M ∖ Z'): ξ(y)(β_δ(y)) = ξ(y)(α̃(y)) + ξ(y)(β_δ(y) − β(y)) ≥ 1 − |β_δ(y) − β(y)| ≥ 1 − ε by step 1(c) and (b). For y ∈ (M ∩ (V ∖ F)) ∖ Z, |χ(y)ξ(y)(β_δ(y))| ≤ 1. Since μ(V ∖ F) ≤ μ(V ∖ K) + μ(K ∖ F) < 2ε, we get T(ω) ≥ (1 − ε)μ(F) − 2ε ≥ (1 − ε)(μ(K) − ε) − 2ε ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3).
 (g) Hence M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(ω) ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3); letting ε ↓ 0 gives M_W(T) ≥ μ(K).
5. Exhaustion. W is open, so W = ⋃_m K_m with the increasing compact sets K_m := {y ∈ W : |y| ≤ m, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ 1/m} (K_m := {|y| ≤ m} if W = ℝ^P). By continuity of μ from below and step 4, μ(W) = sup_m μ(K_m) ≤ M_W(T). Together with step 3, M_W(T) = μ(W) in [0, ∞].
proof_key_steps: A unit simple n-vector ζ satisfies |ζ(α)| ≤ |α|_Euclid (Cauchy–Binet) and has a dual covector α_ζ, linear in ζ, with |α_ζ| = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = 1.
Upper bound: for every admissible ω, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W).
Lower bound on compact K ⊆ W: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, mollification and a cutoff give an admissible ω with T(ω) ≥ μ_R(K) − ε(μ_R(K) + 3).
Exhaust the open set W by compact sets to conclude M_W(T) = μ_R(W).

subproblems.title: Basic properties of the weight measure θHᵏ⌞M of an IMRep: absolute continuity both ways, formula on Borel sets, local finiteness, and R.action ω = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure (reused accepted cbr_imRep_measure_basic)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^P (no openness is assumed) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in W (IMRep W k): M = R.carrier is a Borel set with M ⊆ W, θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable with θ(x) ≥ 1 for x ∈ M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W, and ξ = R.orient : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M; here Hᵏ = μHE[k], R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ (the weight θHᵏ⌞M, contract IMRep.measure) and R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) (contract IMRep.action). Then: (a) R.measure ≪ Hᵏ⌞M; (b) Hᵏ⌞M ≪ R.measure; (c) R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ (lower Lebesgue integral of the [0,∞]-valued cast of θ) for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P; (d) R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0; (e) R.measure(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W; (f) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for R.measure; (g) for every k-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) (an arbitrary DifferentialForm; no smoothness or integrability is assumed), R.action ω = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep W k), R.measure ≪ μHE[k].restrict R.carrier ∧ μHE[k].restrict R.carrier ≪ R.measure ∧ (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ A, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[k]) ∧ R.measure R.carrierᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → R.measure K < ∞) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable R.orient R.measure ∧ ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k, R.action ω = ∫ x, R.orient x (ω x) ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance: comparator-accepted declaration cbr_imRep_measure_basic (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.im_local-a1.imrep_measure-a1, candidate commit d37eb4df), reused with its identical frozen type. The selected parent uses two of its parts.
- Part (d), R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0, together with M ⊆ U (field carrier_subset) and monotonicity, gives R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0. This is the parent's step 3: the carriers lie in U, so μ_•(E) = μ_•(E ∩ U).
- Part (e), R.measure(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, is the local finiteness of the parent's step 4 (IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult).
The numbered proof below is that node's accepted parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim. Its 'Source' line and the phrase 'the selected node' refer to that node's original parent.

Notation: ν := Hᵏ⌞M = μHE[k].restrict M and g(x) := θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞], so that R.measure = ν.withDensity g by the definition IMRep.measure.
1. g is measurable: θ is measurable (field measurable_mult of R), and the cast ℕ → [0, ∞] is measurable because every map out of ℕ is.
2. Proof of (c). Let A be Borel. By the definition of a measure with density, R.measure(A) = ∫_A g dν = ∫ g d(ν⌞A) (Mathlib withDensity_apply, A measurable). Since A is measurable, ν⌞A = (Hᵏ⌞M)⌞A = Hᵏ⌞(A ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ.
3. Proof of (d). ℝ^P ∖ M is Borel because M is (field measurableSet_carrier). By (c), R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = ∫_{M ∩ (ℝ^P∖M)} θ dHᵏ = ∫_∅ θ dHᵏ = 0.
4. Proof of (e). Let K ⊆ W be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so by (c) R.measure(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ, and this is finite by the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R applied to the compact set K ⊆ W.

Now let R.measure(A) = 0 and choose a Borel set A' ⊇ A with R.measure(A') = 0 (a measurable hull). Then ∫_{A'} g dν = 0, so g = 0 holds (ν⌞A')-a.e. (Mathlib lintegral_eq_zero_iff, g measurable). Together with g ≠ 0 ν-a.e. this gives (ν⌞A')(ℝ^P) = 0, i.e. ν(A') = 0, hence ν(A) = 0. So ν ≪ R.measure (this is Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous', whose hypotheses are exactly that g is a.e. measurable and g ≠ 0 ν-a.e.).
7. Proof of (f). ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient). By (a), R.measure ≪ ν, and a.e. strong measurability passes to absolutely continuous measures (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac). Hence ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for R.measure.

A.e. strong measurability of ξ passes from Hᵏ⌞M to R.measure by absolute continuity.

subproblems.title: Comparison of measures from open subsets: if μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, ν is finite on compact subsets of the open set U, and μ(V) ≤ ν(V) for every open V ⊆ U, then μ ≤ ν
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let μ, ν be measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (Mathlib Measure (Euclid P), evaluated on arbitrary subsets as outer measures). Assume (i) μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0; (ii) ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; (iii) μ(V) ≤ ν(V) for every open V ⊆ U. Then μ ≤ ν, i.e. μ(E) ≤ ν(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P (equivalently, for every Borel E). No finiteness of μ on compact sets and no local finiteness of ν near the boundary of U or outside U is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ν K < ∞) → (∀ V : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen V → V ⊆ U → μ V ≤ ν V) → μ ≤ ν
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–6 of the selected parent proof, stated for abstract measures μ (the parent's μ_Z) and ν (the parent's μ_X + μ_Y). These steps extend the open-set inequality μ_Z(V) ≤ μ_X(V) + μ_Y(V) (V ⊆ U open) to all Borel sets "by outer regularity of these locally finite Borel measures". As in the parent's step 5, outer regularity is applied to a finite restriction to V_k. Only the restriction ν⌞V_k is needed, because the parent's step 5(c) uses only the ν-part of λ = (μ_X + μ_Y + μ_Z)⌞V_k. Therefore no finiteness of μ on compact sets is assumed. The outer regularity used is Simon, Ch. 1, Theorem 1.15(1) (book/chapter-01.txt lines 274–285), applied to the finite Borel measure ν⌞V_k on the metric space ℝ^P. The parent's exhaustion of step 4 is written with the extended distance to ℝ^P ∖ U, so the case U = ℝ^P needs no separate treatment.

Hypotheses. U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, and μ, ν are measures on the Borel sets of ℝ^P (Mathlib Measure (Euclid P), evaluated on arbitrary sets as outer measures). They satisfy:
(i) μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0;
(ii) ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U;
(iii) μ(V) ≤ ν(V) for every open V ⊆ U.

Notation. For x ∈ ℝ^P let d(x) := inf{‖x − y‖ : y ∈ ℝ^P ∖ U} ∈ [0, ∞] be the extended distance from x to ℝ^P ∖ U (Mathlib Metric.infEDist x Uᶜ). If U = ℝ^P then d ≡ +∞. In [0, ∞], 1/0 = +∞ and 1/k > 0 for every k ∈ ℕ. For k ∈ ℕ put
V_k := {x ∈ ℝ^P : ‖x‖ < k and 1/k < d(x)},
K_k := {x ∈ ℝ^P : ‖x‖ ≤ k and 1/k ≤ d(x)}.

1. (Topology.) The function d is continuous (it is 1-Lipschitz for the extended metric; Mathlib continuous_infEDist), and so is x ↦ ‖x‖. Hence V_k is open, being the intersection of the strict sublevel set {‖x‖ < k} and the strict superlevel set {d > 1/k}. K_k is closed for the same reason with weak inequalities. K_k ⊆ closedBall(0, k) is bounded, so K_k is compact, since closed bounded subsets of ℝ^P are compact.
2. (K_k ⊆ U and V_k ⊆ K_k.) If x ∉ U, then x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ U, so d(x) = 0 < 1/k and x ∉ K_k; thus K_k ⊆ U. Strict inequalities imply weak ones, so V_k ⊆ K_k ⊆ U.
3. (Monotone exhaustion.) If k ≤ m and x ∈ V_k, then ‖x‖ < k ≤ m and 1/m ≤ 1/k < d(x), so x ∈ V_m; thus (V_k) is increasing. By step 2, ⋃_k V_k ⊆ U. Conversely, let x ∈ U. The set ℝ^P ∖ U is closed and does not contain x, so d(x) > 0 (Mathlib infEDist_pos_iff_notMem_closure). Choose a ∈ ℕ with 1/a < d(x) (possible as d(x) > 0; Mathlib ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt) and b ∈ ℕ with ‖x‖ < b, and let k := max(a, b). Then ‖x‖ < b ≤ k and 1/k ≤ 1/a < d(x), so x ∈ V_k. Hence ⋃_k V_k = U.
4. (Finiteness.) By step 2 and hypothesis (ii) applied to the compact set K_k ⊆ U, ν(V_k) ≤ ν(K_k) < ∞.
5. (Comparison inside V_k.) Fix k and an arbitrary set E ⊆ ℝ^P. Let ν_k := ν⌞V_k. Since V_k is Borel, ν_k(A) = ν(A ∩ V_k) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P. By step 4, ν_k is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^P. Hence it is outer regular: for every A ⊆ ℝ^P and every r > ν_k(A) there is an open O ⊇ A with ν_k(O) < r. This is Simon 1.15(1). In Mathlib, a finite measure on a pseudo-metrizable Borel space is weakly regular (instance WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure), hence outer regular (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt).
We claim μ(E ∩ V_k) ≤ ν(E ∩ V_k). It suffices to show μ(E ∩ V_k) < r for every r ∈ [0, ∞] with ν(E ∩ V_k) < r: if instead ν(E ∩ V_k) < μ(E ∩ V_k), then r := μ(E ∩ V_k) would violate this. So let ν(E ∩ V_k) < r. Then ν_k(E) = ν(E ∩ V_k) < r, so there is an open O ⊇ E with ν(O ∩ V_k) = ν_k(O) < r. The set O ∩ V_k is open (step 1) and contained in V_k ⊆ U (step 2). Hypothesis (iii) and monotonicity of μ give
μ(E ∩ V_k) ≤ μ(O ∩ V_k) ≤ ν(O ∩ V_k) < r.
6. (Concentration on U.) Let E be a Borel set. U is open, hence Borel, so μ(E) = μ(E ∩ U) + μ(E ∖ U). By hypothesis (i), μ(E ∖ U) ≤ μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0. Hence μ(E) = μ(E ∩ U).
7. (Continuity from below.) By step 3, the sets E ∩ V_k increase with k and their union is E ∩ U. By continuity of μ from below (Mathlib Monotone.measure_iUnion), μ(E ∩ U) = sup_k μ(E ∩ V_k). By step 5 and monotonicity of ν, μ(E ∩ V_k) ≤ ν(E ∩ V_k) ≤ ν(E) for every k. With step 6, μ(E) = μ(E ∩ U) ≤ ν(E).
8. (Conclusion.) Step 7 holds for every Borel set E. An inequality between measures may be checked on measurable sets (Mathlib Measure.le_iff), so μ ≤ ν, i.e. μ(E) ≤ ν(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P. ∎

Appendix (verified Lean realization of the numbered proof above; not part of the proof). The declaration below was compiled in this decomposition session with Lean v4.35.0-rc3 and Mathlib 25730c7c. It was placed after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission` in the child comparator scope: inside `namespace GMT.Ch07` with the frozen contract's `open` commands, after its `noncomputable section ... end`. `exact Submission.dtc_bc_lc_measure_le_of_le_on_open` closes the frozen type, and `#print axioms` reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

```lean
theorem Submission.dtc_bc_lc_measure_le_of_le_on_open : ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ν K < ∞) → (∀ V : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen V → V ⊆ U → μ V ≤ ν V) → μ ≤ ν := by
  intro P U μ ν hU hμU hν hle
  -- Steps 1–3: the exhaustion `V k ⊆ K k ⊆ U`, `V` increasing with union `U`
  set V : ℕ → Set (Euclid P) :=
    fun k => {x | ‖x‖ < k ∧ (k : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ < infEDist x Uᶜ} with hVdef
  set K : ℕ → Set (Euclid P) :=
    fun k => {x | ‖x‖ ≤ k ∧ (k : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ≤ infEDist x Uᶜ} with hKdef
  have hVopen : ∀ k, IsOpen (V k) := fun k =>
    (isOpen_lt continuous_norm continuous_const).inter
      (isOpen_lt continuous_const continuous_infEDist)
  have hKcpt : ∀ k, IsCompact (K k) := fun k => by
    refine isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded ?_ ?_
    · exact (isClosed_le continuous_norm continuous_const).inter
        (isClosed_le continuous_const continuous_infEDist)
    · refine (isBounded_closedBall (x := (0 : Euclid P)) (r := (k : ℝ))).subset ?_
      intro x hx
      simpa [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right] using hx.1
  have hKU : ∀ k, K k ⊆ U := fun k x hx => by
    by_contra hxU
    have h0 : infEDist x Uᶜ = 0 := infEDist_zero_of_mem hxU
    have h1 : (k : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ ≤ 0 := h0 ▸ hx.2
    exact (ENNReal.inv_ne_zero.mpr (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top k)) (nonpos_iff_eq_zero.mp h1)
  have hVK : ∀ k, V k ⊆ K k := fun k x hx => ⟨hx.1.le, hx.2.le⟩
  have hVmono : Monotone V := fun k m hkm x hx =>
    ⟨lt_of_lt_of_le hx.1 (by exact_mod_cast hkm),
      lt_of_le_of_lt (ENNReal.inv_le_inv.mpr (by exact_mod_cast hkm)) hx.2⟩
  have hVU : ⋃ k, V k = U := by
    apply subset_antisymm
    · exact iUnion_subset fun k => (hVK k).trans (hKU k)
    · intro x hx
      have hpos : 0 < infEDist x Uᶜ := by
        rw [infEDist_pos_iff_notMem_closure, hU.isClosed_compl.closure_eq]
        exact fun h => h hx
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt hpos.ne'
      obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := exists_nat_gt ‖x‖
      refine mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨max a b, ?_, ?_⟩
      · exact lt_of_lt_of_le hb (by exact_mod_cast le_max_right a b)
      · exact lt_of_le_of_lt (ENNReal.inv_le_inv.mpr (by exact_mod_cast le_max_left a b)) ha
  -- Step 4: `ν (V k) < ∞`
  have hνV : ∀ k, ν (V k) ≠ ∞ := fun k =>
    ne_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt (measure_mono (hVK k)) (hν _ (hKcpt k) (hKU k)))
  -- Step 5: comparison inside `V k`, by outer regularity of the finite measure `ν⌞V k`
  have hcomp : ∀ k (E : Set (Euclid P)), μ (E ∩ V k) ≤ ν (E ∩ V k) := by
    intro k E
    have : IsFiniteMeasure (ν.restrict (V k)) := isFiniteMeasure_restrict.mpr (hνV k)
    refine le_of_forall_gt fun r hr => ?_
    rw [← Measure.restrict_apply' (hVopen k).measurableSet] at hr
    obtain ⟨O, hEO, hO, hOr⟩ := Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt E r hr
    rw [Measure.restrict_apply' (hVopen k).measurableSet] at hOr
    calc μ (E ∩ V k) ≤ μ (O ∩ V k) := measure_mono (inter_subset_inter_left _ hEO)
      _ ≤ ν (O ∩ V k) := hle _ (hO.inter (hVopen k))
          (inter_subset_right.trans ((hVK k).trans (hKU k)))
      _ < r := hOr
  -- Steps 6–8: concentration on `U`, continuity from below, `Measure.le_iff`
  rw [Measure.le_iff]
  intro E hE
  calc μ E = μ (E ∩ U) := by
        have h := measure_inter_add_sdiff E hU.measurableSet (μ := μ)
        have h2 : μ (E \ U) = 0 := measure_mono_null (fun x hx => hx.2) hμU
        rw [h2, add_zero] at h
        exact h.symm
    _ = ⨆ k, μ (E ∩ V k) := by
        rw [← hVU, inter_iUnion]
        exact Monotone.measure_iUnion fun k m hkm => inter_subset_inter_right E (hVmono hkm)
    _ ≤ ν E := iSup_le fun k => (hcomp k E).trans (measure_mono inter_subset_left)
```
proof_key_steps: Exhaust U by the open sets V_k = {‖x‖ < k, 1/k < d(x, ℝ^P ∖ U)} (extended distance). They increase with union U, and each lies in the compact set K_k = {‖x‖ ≤ k, 1/k ≤ d(x, ℝ^P ∖ U)} ⊆ U, so ν(V_k) < ∞ by (ii).
ν⌞V_k is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^P, hence outer regular (Simon 1.15(1); Mathlib WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure).
For any E and open O ⊇ E, μ(E ∩ V_k) ≤ μ(O ∩ V_k) ≤ ν(O ∩ V_k) by (iii), since O ∩ V_k ⊆ U is open. Outer regularity of ν⌞V_k then gives μ(E ∩ V_k) ≤ ν(E ∩ V_k).
For Borel E: μ(E) = μ(E ∩ U) by (i), μ(E ∩ U) = sup_k μ(E ∩ V_k) by continuity from below, and this is ≤ ν(E). Measure.le_iff gives μ ≤ ν.
